summary: Beckett is a Pirate lord that steals one nonland permanent per end step from a player hit by three different Pirates. This review re-verifies the retrospective attestation (Roaming Throne doubling, Open into Wonder, turn-history condition). It adds the type-changing steal package (Don Andres, Coercive Recruiter, Zara, Hostage Taker), the changelings, the one-sided sweepers and Double Down's legend-rule interaction. Flag: Kari Zev's Ragavan token is a Monkey, not a Pirate, so it never counts toward the three. No combos: the deck is a value and control engine.

interactions.title: Three different Pirates, same player, combat damage, this turn
interactions.ruling: The end-step trigger targets a nonland permanent controlled by a player who was dealt combat damage by three or more *different* Pirates this turn. A double striker counts once. Damage over several combat phases (Port Razer) adds up. The condition is turn history: the Pirates needn't still be on the battlefield or still be Pirates, and Beckett needn't have been out when they connected. If no player qualifies, there is no legal target and the trigger does nothing. The theft lasts indefinitely, even after Beckett leaves.
interactions.short: Three different Pirates must deal combat damage to the same player; history counts, theft is permanent.

oracle.quote: At the beginning of your end step, gain control of target nonland permanent controlled by a player who was dealt combat damage by three or more Pirates this turn.

rulings.quote: If one Pirate deals combat damage multiple times, most likely because it has double strike, it counts as only one of the three Pirates for Admiral Beckett Brass's triggered ability.
It doesn't care whether Admiral Beckett Brass was on the battlefield when those Pirates dealt combat damage, whether those creatures are still on the battlefield, or whether they're still Pirates.
The control-change effect of Admiral Beckett Brass's triggered ability lasts indefinitely.

source.quote: the permanents need not still be on the battlefield at the end step for the turn-history condition to have happened.

interactions.title: One target, even if several players qualify
interactions.ruling: If two players were each hit by three Pirates, Beckett still takes one permanent from either of them. With Roaming Throne naming Pirate, Beckett is 'another creature of the chosen type', so his trigger triggers an additional time. Each instance picks its own target, so you can take two permanents, from one player or from two.
interactions.short: One steal per trigger; Roaming Throne (Pirate) makes it two, with separate targets.

oracle.quote: If a triggered ability of another creature you control of the chosen type triggers, it triggers an additional time.

rulings.quote: If more than one player was dealt combat damage by three Pirates, you target only one permanent.
Any choices made as you put the ability onto the stack, such as modes and targets, are made separately for each instance of the ability.

source.quote: `Roaming Throne` choosing Pirate causes a triggered ability of another Pirate creature you control to trigger an additional time

interactions.title: Kari Zev's Ragavan token is a Monkey, not a Pirate
interactions.ruling: Kari Zev's token is 'Ragavan, a legendary 2/1 red Monkey'. It isn't a Pirate, so it doesn't count toward Beckett's three and doesn't get his +1/+1. It enters attacking but was never declared as an attacker, so attack triggers don't see it. The card Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer (Monkey Pirate) has a different name, so the two can coexist under the legend rule.

flag.note: Easy miscount: the Ragavan token never counts as one of Beckett's three Pirates. Count Kari Zev herself, not her token.

oracle.quote: create Ragavan, a legendary 2/1 red Monkey creature token

rulings.quote: Although Ragavan is attacking, it was never declared as an attacking creature

interactions.title: Don Andres and Coercive Recruiter turn stolen creatures into Pirates
interactions.ruling: Don Andres makes each creature you control but don't own a Pirate, with +2/+2, menace and deathtouch. That covers Hostage Taker casts, Zara's hand-stolen attacker and Coercive Recruiter steals. Coercive Recruiter also makes its own target a Pirate with haste until end of turn. These creatures count toward Beckett's three when they deal combat damage. Tokens you create are owned by you, so Don Andres doesn't affect them.
interactions.short: Stolen creatures become Pirates (Don Andres, Coercive Recruiter) and count for Beckett.

oracle.quote: Each creature you control but don't own gets +2/+2, has menace and deathtouch, and is a Pirate in addition to its other types.
Until end of turn, it gains haste and becomes a Pirate in addition to its other types.

rulings.quote: The player who creates a token is its owner.

interactions.title: Zara's stolen attacker counts but skips attack triggers
interactions.ruling: Zara puts a creature from the defending player's hand onto the battlefield tapped and attacking. It wasn't declared as an attacker, so Breeches, Dire Fleet Captain and Fathom Fleet Captain don't trigger for it. With Don Andres out it's a Pirate and counts for Beckett if it connects. It returns to its owner's hand at the next end step, but Beckett's history check doesn't care.

oracle.quote: You may put a creature card from it onto the battlefield under your control tapped and attacking that player or a planeswalker they control.

rulings.quote: Although the creature is attacking, it was never declared as an attacking creature.

interactions.title: Changelings count as Pirates
interactions.ruling: Changeling makes an object every creature type in every zone. Changeling Outcast (can't block, can't be blocked) and the Shapeshifter token from Black Market Connections' 'Hire a Mercenary' mode are Pirates. They get Beckett's +1/+1 and count toward his three. They survive Fiery Cannonade and Raise the Palisade (choosing Pirate).

oracle.quote: This creature can't block and can't be blocked.
Create a 3/2 colorless Shapeshifter creature token with changeling.

interactions.title: One-sided sweepers: Fiery Cannonade and Raise the Palisade
interactions.ruling: Fiery Cannonade deals 2 to each non-Pirate creature. Raise the Palisade naming Pirate bounces every non-Pirate. Your survivors are your Pirates, changelings, a Roaming Throne that named Pirate, and stolen creatures made Pirates by Don Andres or Coercive Recruiter. Kari Zev's Monkey token is hit by both. Beckett's +1/+1 doesn't protect a 1-toughness non-Pirate.

oracle.quote: Fiery Cannonade deals 2 damage to each non-Pirate creature.
Return all creatures that aren't of the chosen type to their owners' hands.

interactions.title: Double Down copies Pirate spells; legendary copies hit the legend rule
interactions.ruling: Double Down copies each outlaw spell you cast, and Pirates are outlaws. The copy resolves first and becomes a token. For nonlegendary Pirates that's a second body with its own enter-the-battlefield trigger: a second Hostage Taker exile, or a Coercive Recruiter steal. For legendary Pirates (Ramirez, Breeches, Kari Zev, Malcolm, Zara, Edward Kenway, Admiral Brass, Beckett himself), the original then resolves and the legend rule makes you keep one. Both enter-the-battlefield triggers still happen; Ramirez makes 4 Treasures and you lose 4 life. A copy isn't cast, so it doesn't count for cast triggers. Double Down doesn't trigger on Pirates put onto the battlefield without being cast.
interactions.short: Double Down copies Pirate spells; a legendary copy means a legend-rule choice, but both ETBs happen.

oracle.quote: Whenever you cast an outlaw spell, copy that spell.

rulings.quote: Double Down's ability and the copy it creates will resolve before the spell that caused it to trigger.
Double Down's ability doesn't trigger if an outlaw permanent is put onto the battlefield without being cast.

interactions.title: Roaming Throne naming Pirate doubles the deck's Pirate triggers
interactions.ruling: Roaming Throne (choose Pirate, so it's a Pirate too) makes triggered abilities of your *other* Pirate creatures trigger an additional time. That doubles Beckett's end step, Admiral Brass's combat reanimation and Coercive Recruiter's steal. Merchant Raiders taps a second target, and Forerunner's life loss doubles. Breeches, Eager Pillager triggers twice per attacking Pirate, but there are only three modes per turn, so the extra trigger may have no mode left to choose. Only abilities of creatures are doubled, so Double Down and Kindred Discovery aren't.
interactions.uncertainty: With Breeches, Eager Pillager, an extra trigger after all three modes have been chosen that turn has no legal mode. The CR on modal triggers whose modes are used up applies, but no card-specific ruling confirms it.

oracle.quote: This creature is the chosen type in addition to its other types.

rulings.quote: Roaming Throne's last ability doesn't copy the triggered ability; it just causes the ability to trigger an additional time.

interactions.title: Port Razer extra combats and Beckett's tally
interactions.ruling: Port Razer connecting untaps all your creatures and adds a combat phase after the current one. Pirates that dealt damage in the first combat still count for Beckett. A second combat lets different Pirates hit the same player and complete the three. Port Razer itself can't attack a player it already attacked this turn, and it never has to attack.

oracle.quote: After this phase, there is an additional combat phase.

rulings.quote: Port Razer doesn't have to attack in any additional combat it creates (or any other time for that matter).

interactions.title: Open into Wonder and evasion only enable; damage must happen
interactions.ruling: Open into Wonder (X creatures can't be blocked) and Cover of Darkness (choose Pirate: fear) get Pirates through, but Beckett still needs actual combat damage. Prevention or a creature removed before damage means it doesn't count.

oracle.quote: X target creatures can't be blocked this turn.

source.quote: the resulting Beckett condition still depends on actual combat damage.

interactions.title: The Indomitable is cast from the graveyard with tapped Pirates
interactions.ruling: The Indomitable can be cast from your graveyard while you control three or more tapped Pirates and/or Vehicles. That is checked only as you begin casting, so post-combat after a three-Pirate attack is the natural window. You still pay its cost. It needs crew 3 to attack. Its combat-damage draw triggers for any creature you control, not only Vehicles.

oracle.quote: You may cast this card from your graveyard as long as you control three or more tapped Pirates and/or Vehicles.

rulings.quote: The Indomitable checks if you control three or more tapped Pirates and/or Vehicles only as you begin to cast it.

interactions.title: End-step pile-up: Beckett, Edward Kenway, Daring Piracy, Zara, dash

oracle.quote: At the beginning of your end step, create a Treasure token for each tapped Assassin, Pirate, and/or Vehicle you control.

rulings.quote: If a tapped permanent you control has more than one of the subtypes listed in Edward’s first ability, count it only once when determining how many Treasure tokens to create.

interactions.title: Beckett's anthem, Admiral Brass's base 4/4 and the lords
interactions.ruling: Admiral Brass sets a reanimated Pirate's base power and toughness to 4/4 (layer 7b). Beckett's and Corsair Captain's +1/+1 apply afterwards (layer 7c), so the creature is 6/6 with both lords. Counters also apply on top. The finality counter exiles it if it would die.

oracle.quote: Other Pirates you control get +1/+1.
It has base power and toughness 4/4.

rulings.quote: Effects that otherwise modify the returned creature's power and toughness will still apply no matter when they took effect.

interactions.title: Commander tax and the 4-mana commander
interactions.ruling: Beckett costs {1}{U}{B}{R}, then 6, then 8. Fierce Guardianship and Deflecting Swat are free and Jeska's Will gets both modes only while you control a commander, so they get worse while Beckett is off the battlefield. Beckett has no protection of his own: Lightning Greaves (shroud) and Siren Stormtamer cover him.

oracle.quote: If you control a commander, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost.
Equipped creature has haste and shroud.

rulings.quote: It doesn't matter whose commander you control. Any one will do.

interactions.title: What the list depends on
interactions.ruling: The plan needs three Pirates connecting with the same player in one turn. Evasion density is high: flyers, menace, unblockable, fear via Cover of Darkness, Open into Wonder. Interaction is light on fogs and blockers. Mass blockers or fogs stop the steal for a turn but don't disable the board. Stealing a permanent is the main value; the deck has no deterministic two-card combo (Spellbook lists none).
